title: Truth Tables and Digital Logic Gates in Modern Physics
short_intro: Truth tables are exhaustive mathematical tables that display all possible input logic combinations for a logic gate or digital circuit alongside their corresponding binary output. They form the foundational basis for analyzing combinational logic circuits in digital electronics.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR) and their truth tables, Boolean algebra basics, and simple symbol identification.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Universal gates (NAND and NOR), XOR and XNOR gates, De Morgan's theorems, and complex combinational logic network analysis.

prerequisites: Basic semiconductor diode and transistor switching behavior

concept_notes.heading: Fundamental Logic Gates (AND, OR, NOT)
bullets: The NOT gate (inverter) takes a single input A and produces an output Y = Ā, inverting the logic state.
The AND gate produces a HIGH output (1) if and only if all of its inputs are HIGH, expressed as Y = A • B.
The OR gate produces a HIGH output (1) if at least one of its inputs is HIGH, expressed as Y = A + B.

concept_notes.heading: Universal Gates (NAND and NOR)
bullets: A NAND gate is a combination of an AND gate followed by a NOT gate, yielding an output Y = A • B̄.
A NOR gate is a combination of an OR gate followed by a NOT gate, yielding an output Y = A + B̄.
Both NAND and NOR gates are termed universal gates because any boolean function or logic gate can be implemented entirely using either type alone.

concept_notes.heading: Exclusive-OR (XOR) and Exclusive-NOR (XNOR) Gates
bullets: The XOR gate produces a HIGH output when the number of HIGH inputs is odd, acting as a controlled inverter or binary adder component.
The XNOR gate produces a HIGH output when all inputs are identical (even number of 1s), functioning as an equality detector.
Boolean expression for two-input XOR is Y = ĀB + AB̄ and for XNOR is Y = AB + ĀB̄.

concept_notes.heading: Boolean Laws and Simplification via Truth Tables
bullets: Truth tables verify Boolean identities such as De Morgan's laws: (A + B)̄ = Ā • B̄ and (A • B)̄ = Ā + B̄.
Any combinational logic circuit with n binary inputs requires 2ⁿ rows in its truth table to map every possible input combination.
Logic minimization using truth tables ensures optimal hardware implementation with minimum gate count.

derivations.title: Equivalence of NAND Gate as a Universal NOT Gate
derivations.conditions: All inputs of an n-input NAND gate are tied together to a single input A.
steps: Let a 2-input NAND gate have inputs connected together such that A = B.
The standard output equation for a NAND gate is Y = overline{A cdot B}.
Substitute B = A into the equation: Y = overline{A cdot A}.
Using Boolean idempotent law (A • A = A), the equation simplifies to Y = overline{A}.
derivations.result: A multi-input NAND gate with shorted inputs functions identically to a NOT gate.

derivations.title: De Morgan's First Law Verification via Truth Table
derivations.conditions: Two binary variables A and B evaluated across all four input combinations.
steps: Construct a truth table with columns for A, B, A + B, overline{A+B}, overline{A}, overline{B}, and overline{A}cdotoverline{B}.
Evaluate A + B for all combinations (0,0; 0,1; 1,0; 1,1) and invert to get overline{A+B}.
Independently evaluate overline{A} and overline{B} and compute their logical AND product overline{A}cdotoverline{B}.
Compare the output column of overline{A+B} with the column of overline{A}cdotoverline{B} row by row.
derivations.result: Both columns yield identical output values {1, 0, 0, 0}, proving overline{A + B} = overline{A} cdot overline{B}.

formula_sheet.name: XOR Gate Boolean Relation
formula_sheet.equation_html: Y = A oplus B = overline{A}B + Aoverline{B}

formula_sheet.name: XNOR Gate Boolean Relation
formula_sheet.equation_html: Y = overline{A oplus B} = AB + overline{A}overline{B}

formula_sheet.name: Combinational Rows Formula
formula_sheet.variables: n = Number of independent input variables, N_rows = Total rows in truth table

graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Plot of Output Voltage (V_out) versus Input Voltage (V_in) showing sharp transition region between logic LOW and logic HIGH thresholds.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Demonstrates noise margin and threshold voltage (V_IL and V_IH) where the transistor switches state.

solved_numericals.question: Identify the output Y of a two-input NAND gate when input A = 1 and input B = 0.
solution_steps: Recall the Boolean expression for a NAND gate: Y = overline{A cdot B}.
Substitute the given values: A = 1 and B = 0 into the expression.
Apply the NOT operation: Y = overline{0} = 1.

solved_numericals.question: How many rows are present in the truth table of a combinational logic circuit having 4 independent binary inputs?
solution_steps: Identify the number of input variables: n = 4.
Apply the formula for total truth table rows: N = 2^{n}.

solved_numericals.question: Using Boolean algebra and truth table verification, simplify the expression Y = AB + A(B + C) + B(B + C).
solution_steps: Expand terms using distributive law: Y = AB + AB + AC + BB + BC.
Apply idempotent laws (AB + AB = AB and BB = B): Y = AB + AC + B + BC.
Apply absorption law on B + BC (since B + BC = B(1 + C) = B): Y = AB + AC + B.
Apply absorption law on AB + B (since B + AB = B): Y = B + AC.

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumes ideal binary logic levels where voltages strictly represent discrete states 0 (0 V) and 1 (+5 V or +V_cc), ignoring transient voltage fluctuations and noise margins in real physical hardware.

common_misconceptions.wrong: A truth table can only have inputs represented by numerical values without physical meaning.
common_misconceptions.correct: Truth tables represent abstract binary logic states that correspond directly to physical voltage levels or switch positions in circuits.
common_misconceptions.why: Digital abstraction bridges mathematical logic with semiconductor electronics.

common_misconceptions.wrong: NAND and NOR gates are called universal gates because they are cheaper to manufacture.
common_misconceptions.correct: They are called universal gates because any Boolean function can be implemented exclusively using either NAND or NOR gates alone.
common_misconceptions.why: Universality is a functional property derived from functional completeness in logic.

quick_revision: AND gate outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1; OR gate outputs 0 only when all inputs are 0.
NOT Gate Boolean Relation: Y = overline{A}
AND Gate Boolean Relation: Y = A cdot B
